build: The project builds with Cargo; CI (.github/workflows/rust.yml) runs `cargo build --verbose` on every push and pull request.
build_common_tools: Builds use Cargo, the standard and widely-adopted Rust build toolchain.
build_floss_tools: All build and CI tooling is FLOSS: Cargo/rustc, GitHub Actions, clippy, and cargo-deny.
contribution_requirements: CONTRIBUTING.md documents forking, PRs against `master`, the PR template, dev setup, the testing requirement, and Conventional Commits.
crypto_call: Outbound internet calls (GitHub API for version checks/downloads) use HTTPS via the system `curl`, which negotiates TLS — no plaintext internet communication.
crypto_floss: TLS is provided by the system `curl`/OS libraries (FLOSS); the project bundles no proprietary cryptography.
crypto_keylength: Relies on `curl`/OS TLS defaults (modern ciphers with >=128-bit security and standard RSA/ECDSA key sizes).
crypto_pfs: Modern TLS via `curl` negotiates forward secrecy (ECDHE) with current GitHub endpoints.
crypto_published: Uses the widely-published TLS protocol through the standard `curl` toolchain rather than any custom or unpublished algorithm.
crypto_random: The project generates no security-sensitive random values (only UUIDs for internal job IDs), so no cryptographic RNG is required for its functionality.
crypto_working: TLS HTTPS calls to GitHub succeed in practice; the version-check and self-update features work as designed.
enhancement_responses: Enhancement requests are tracked on the public GitHub issue tracker (with a feature-request template) and reviewed through PRs.
no_leaked_credentials: Sensitive local config (config/mt5-quant.yaml, which can hold passwords/tokens) is gitignored, and no secrets are committed to the repository.
repo_interim: The repository at github.com/masdevid/mt5-quant is the canonical project home, not a temporary or interim placeholder.
report_archive: GitHub automatically archives the source; tagged releases additionally publish downloadable source and binary archives.
report_responses: The project uses GitHub Issues (with bug/feature templates) as its public tracker, and maintainers triage and respond via issues and PR reviews.
static_analysis: CI runs Rust Clippy and GitHub CodeQL (Rust) as static analysis on every push and pull request.
static_analysis_fixed: Clippy runs with `-D warnings` so defects fail the build, and CodeQL findings are reviewed and remediated.
static_analysis_often: Static analysis runs automatically on every push to and pull request against `master` (clippy in rust.yml, CodeQL in codeql.yml).
test: Unit and integration tests exist in `tests/` (Rust integration_tests.rs, test_mcp.py, shell tests) and `cargo test` runs in CI.
test_most: Unit tests cover core modules (analytics extraction/analysis, storage, report parsing); `cargo test` is part of CI.
test_policy: AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md require that non-trivial changes include tests, and CI enforces `cargo test`.
tests_are_added: The `tests/` directory contains Rust, Python, and shell tests, and new non-trivial functionality is expected to add corresponding tests.
tests_documented_added: Testing expectations and the `cargo test` requirement are documented in AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md.
version_semver: The `version` field in Cargo.toml uses Semantic Versioning (currently 1.34.3).
version_tags: Releases are tagged with `vX.Y.Z` semver tags (e.g., v1.34.1), confirmed via `git tag`.
version_unique: Each release carries a unique `version` in Cargo.toml and a corresponding immutable `vX.Y.Z` git tag.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed: No known unpatched critical vulnerabilities; `cargo-deny` advisories and dependency-review run in CI and dependency updates are monitored.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days: Dependency vulnerabilities are surfaced by `cargo-deny` (advisories) and the dependency-review action in CI, and are updated promptly.
warnings: CI enforces a warning-free build via `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` plus `cargo fmt --check`.
warnings_fixed: Because Clippy uses `-D warnings`, any warning fails CI and must be fixed before a change can merge.
dynamic_analysis: Dynamic analysis is performed via cargo-fuzz (libFuzzer) fuzz targets in fuzz/ that exercise the report/metrics parsers with arbitrary input.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions: The cargo-fuzz build enables debug/overflow assertions: fuzz/Cargo.toml sets `[profile.release] debug-assertions = true` (and `[profile.dev] debug-assertions = true`), so debug_assert! checks and integer-overflow traps remain active while libFuzzer feeds arbitrary input; crashes that violate internal invariants are caught as bugs.
dynamic_analysis_fixed: Fuzzing findings are triaged and fixed; crashes found by the harness are treated as bugs.
